name: Pipy
workload: HTTP GET echo/hello-world with wrk (100 concurrent, 1 connection thread, 20s) on a 2 vCPU ARM64 VM, Ubuntu 21 and FreeBSD 13
claimed_speedup: wrk on ubuntu21-arm64: Pipy 218539 req/s vs nginx 82759 req/s (~2.6x, derived from page data)
hardware: 2 vCPU / 4GB ARM64 VM (Ubuntu 21 Server and FreeBSD 13, ARM64); no CPU model stated
tradeoffs: Pipy is a programmable proxy (scriptable via PipyJS), not a drop-in nginx replacement; nginx was run with only 1 worker in this test which is not how nginx is typically deployed in production
caveats: First-party benchmark (project's own wiki), partial methodology: no compiler/build flags stated and no exact CPU model given (only vCPU count and 'ARM64'), so capped at tier C per rules even though numbers and test scripts are public. wrk latency P90/P99 ratios also given but headline metric used here is throughput.
found_via: Hacker News: "HTTP server benchmark C++" -> story 30827766 "HTTP Echo server benchmark, Nginx(C), HTTP-echo(go), Pipy(C++)" linking to the wiki benchmark page
